sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH (2021)
cleanIntro: Traditions asks for this after every shooting session. The Pursuit XT is a break-open inline: the barrel comes off the frame and the Accelerator Breech Plug comes out of the barrel, which is what lets you clean the bore from the breech end instead of dragging fouling the length of it.

steps.title: Treat it as loaded
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction and handle it as a loaded gun before you touch anything else.
steps.quote: WARNING: ALWAYS POINT THE PURSUIT™ XT IN A SAFE DIRECTION AND TREAT THE PURSUIT™ XT AS IF IT WAS LOADED AND CAN FIRE. WARNING: CONFIRM THE PURSUIT™ XT IS UNLOADED BEFORE CONDUCTING ANY OF THE METHODS IN THIS SECTION. WARNING: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE YOUR PURSUIT™ XT ANY FURTHER THAN WHAT IS DESCRIBED IN THIS MANUAL. Disassembling your Pursuit™ XT further could cause the firearm to become unsafe. As a result, it could cause serious injury and/or death to the shooter or bystanders and could damage the Pursuit™ XT. WARNING: CONFIRM NO POWDER CHARGES, PRIMERS, OR PROJECTILES ARE PRESENT OR AVAILABLE DURING ANY DISASSEMBLY, CLEANING, OR REASSEMBLY. NOTE: Reference to the exploded view diagram in the manual will help identify part names and numbers. RANGE/FIELD CLEANING AND ADVICE WHILE SHOOTING A systematic routine of cleaning while shooting is strongly advised to aid in avoiding problems while loading and to optimize accuracy. When target shooting or sighting in, develop a habit of consistenly cleaning your barrel after each shot. Depending upon the specific load, temperature, and humidity, a short series of shots with black powder or black powder substitute can be fired before it becomes necessary to clean your barrel and remove fouling build-up. Suggested Method Make sure the Pursuit™ XT is uncharged and unloaded. The safety should be in the "safe" position so no red ring is visible and should always be pointed in a safe direction. With the action open, take a Traditions® dry patch and saturate it in bore solvent (or you can use a pre-saturated cleaning patch.) Traditions® suggests using a Traditions® Range Rod but you can also use the ramrod that comes with the Pursuit™ XT with the jag flipped around to elongate the rod. Place the patch over the end of your rod and insert it into the muzzle end of the Pursuit XT™. Run the patch up and down to remove any fouling. Remove the saturated patch and discard. Place a dry patch over the end of the rod and run the dry patch from the muzzle to the breech to remove any moisture. Do this until the patch is clean. Repeat this process as many times as necessary until your barrel is clean. The same process should be repeated going from the breech. Repeat as necessary to remove fouling. © 2021 Traditions® Performance Firearms. All Rights Reserved. 36 NOTE: A dirty fouled barrel will directly affect your ability to group shots. However, in a hunting situation, only a few shots will likely be taken. If the barrel is prepped and lubed at the onset, it is not necessary to clean and lube the interior of the barrel between shots when hunting. ADDITIONAL RANGE CLEANING ADVICE NOTE: It should never be necessary to hammer or excessively force a projectile down the bore. Projectiles should load firmly with pressure from the ramrod down the barrel. If the projectile is the proper size, unusual resistance usually indicates a need to clean the bore. 1. Do not use shooting patches when cleaning your Pursuit™ XT. They are too small. You should use Traditions® cleaning patches. 2. If a patch gets stuck, use Traditions Patch Puller Worm attached to a ramrod for retrieval, or if necessary, remove the breech plug and push the patch out through the breech area. Never load a charge over a lost patch. 3. If unusual resistance is felt while loading your projectile, perform the suggested cleaning method to remove as much of the fouling build up as possible. 4. If for any reason the projectile will not go all the way down to the powder charge, it will be necessary to extract the projectile from the barrel either with a bullet puller on a ramrod or the breech plug can be removed, the charge removed and the projectile forced out the end of the barrel with a long bench/range rod or an extended ramrod. NOTE: It should never be necessary to hammer or excessively force a projectile down the bore. Projectiles should load firmly against the powder charge with a series of short strokes. If the projectile is the proper size, unusual resistance usually indicates the need to swab the bore with a treated cleaning patch. Use cleaning solvent if barrel is heavily fouled. An occasional cleaning of the bore with a brass Traditions® Bore Brush is advisable to remove excessive plastic and fouling build-up. © 2021 Traditions® Performance Firearms. All Rights Reserved. 37 18. DISASSEMBLY, DETAILED CLEANING, & REASSEMBLY WARNING: ALWAYS POINT THE PURSUIT™ XT IN A SAFE DIRECTION AND TREAT THE PURSUIT™ XT AS IF IT WAS LOADED AND CAN FIRE. WARNING: CONFIRM THE PURSUIT™ XT IS UNCHARGED AND UNPRIMED BEFORE CONDUCTING ANY OF THE METHODS IN THIS SECTION.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.38
steps.warn: Uncharged and unprimed are two separate checks. A muzzleloader with the primer off can still hold a full charge and a seated bullet.

steps.title: Engage the safety
steps.action: Push the safety across until the red ring disappears. Red showing means the rifle is in the fire position.
steps.quote: 1. Follow all safety rules listed previously in this manual. Be sure the safety is engaged so it is in the "safe" position and the red ring is not visible.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.38

steps.title: Prove the bore is empty with the ramrod
steps.action: Flip the jag to the far end of the ramrod to lengthen it, run it down the bore, and read where it stops against the muzzle.
steps.prose: The 3/4" mark is the whole test: a rod that stands proud of the muzzle is sitting on a bullet, not on the breech face.
steps.quote: 2. To check if the muzzleloader is unloaded, remove the ramrod and unscrew the jag. Re-attach at the opposite end of the jag. Place the ramrod down the barrel. The fully extended ramrod should sit 3/4" below the muzzle on an unloaded rifle. If your ramrod extends beyond the muzzle, you will need to disassemble the muzzleloader and remove the obstructions before proceeding.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.38

steps.title: Open the action and back out the breech plug
steps.action: Depress the barrel catch lever, then unscrew the Accelerator Breech Plug out of the breech.
steps.caution: If the plug will not turn, the manual's remedy is a soak and a padded vise — not more leverage on a dry plug.
steps.quote: 3. Open rifle by depressing the barrel catch lever and remove Accelerator Breech Plug. NOTE: Remove the barrel from the frame Pour some hot water into the barrel and let it soak for about a 1/2 hour. Secure the barrel in a padded vise. Position the wrench onto the breech plug and remove. Be careful not to scald yourself with the hot water. If you don't have access to hot water, as an alternative you could spray penetrating oil down the muzzle and let it sit for 1 hour and then cotninue by putting it in the vise.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.39

steps.title: Inspect the open breech
steps.action: With the plug out, look and feel through the breech to confirm nothing is left in the barrel.
steps.quote: 4. Inspect the barrel to be sure your rifle is unprimed, unloaded, and free of obstruction.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.39

steps.title: Remove the forend screw
steps.action: Back the forend stock screw out of the barrel assembly with the 4mm Allen wrench.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the forend stock screw from the barrel assembly using the 4mm Allen wrench.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.39

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Push the barrel catch lever in and lift the barrel clear of the frame. Barrel, frame and breech plug are now the three pieces you clean.
steps.quote: 6. Remove the barrel from the frame by pushing the barrel catch lever in. 7. When the barrel starts to open, lift the barrel out of the frame. You can now clean your barrel and frame. Field disassembly is now complete.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.39

steps.title: Wet the bore and let the solvent work
steps.action: Run a solvent-charged bronze brush into the bore and leave the solvent to sit before you scrub.
steps.prose: Fifteen minutes of dwell does more than fifteen strokes of a dry brush. Black powder fouling is water-soluble crust, not carbon lacquer.
steps.quote: 2. Spray a bore solvent, such as Traditions® EZ Clean 2 or BlackOut 209 solvent, on your bronze brush. Note: Traditions® Foaming Bore Solvent can also be used instead of spraying the bore solvent on the bronze brush. Allow solvent to sit for 15 minutes inside the barrel. This will allow time for the solvent to engage and penetrate the fouling. Do not let it dry.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.40

steps.title: Scrub breech to muzzle
steps.action: Push the bronze brush in from the breech end and out at the muzzle, then draw it back.
steps.aside: Working from the breech is possible on this rifle only because the plug is out — that is why the strip comes first.
steps.quote: 4. To clean your barrel, insert your bronze brush into the breech area. Push the ramrod from the breech to the muzzle until the brush exits the muzzle. Pull the ramrod back through the barrel towards the breech. The technique allows you to help break up fouling.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.40

steps.title: Patch it dry
steps.action: Swap the brush for the jag and run dry patches from the breech until they come out clean.
steps.quote: 6. Place a dry cotton patch over the jag and insert it into the breech. Run the ramrod with the patch from the breech to the muzzle. Pull the ramrod back through to the muzzle. Repeat until patch comes out clean.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.40

steps.title: Leave a protective film
steps.action: Finish with a seasoning or lightly lubed patch pushed from the muzzle back to the breech.
steps.quote: 7. Using a Traditions® Cleaning & Seasoning Patch or some gun lube on a dry patch, place the patch over the cleaning jag and insert into the muzzle. Push the patch from the muzzle to the breech. This will help protect against rust and allow for easier loading.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.40

deepSteps.title: Soak and scrub the breech plug
deepSteps.action: Get solvent inside and outside the plug, then brush the threads and the fire channel until nothing more comes off.
deepSteps.prose: The fire channel is the small hole the primer flame travels down. A plugged channel is the single most common cause of a misfire on this action.
deepSteps.quote: 3. To clean your breech plug, spray the breech plug inside and out with solvent or drop the breech plug into the EZ Clean™ parts bath system to loosen the residue and fouling on the plug. Let the solvent sit or if using the parts bath method, let the breech plug sit in the solvent for 10 minutes. Use a stiff brush to clean the outside threads and inner area of the breech plug including the fire channel. A pipe cleaner can be used to get the smaller areas clean and dry. Wipe with a clean cotton cloth. Repeat until all residues are off.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.40

deepSteps.title: Clean the barrel lug and pivot
deepSteps.action: Solvent the lug, wipe it off, and use the nylon brush where the catch and pivot are packed with fouling.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Lightly spray the barrel lug with Traditions® Cleaning Solvent. Wipe the solvent off with a dry cotton cleaning patch. If these areas are heavily fouled use the nylon brush to help remove fouling from the barrel catch and pivot points.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.41

deepSteps.title: Oil the barrel exterior and extractor
deepSteps.action: Wipe a light film of gun oil over every outside metal surface, extractor included.
deepSteps.quote: 9. Apply a light coating of gun oil to the outside of the barrel and all metal surfaces including the extractor.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.41

deepSteps.title: Clean inside the frame
deepSteps.action: Spray the frame interior, brush or patch the fouling out of the frame face and barrel catch, then dry it.
deepSteps.quote: 10. To clean the inside of the frame, lightly spray cleaning solvent on the inside of the frame. Use the Nylon Brush or a dry patch to remove fouling. Be sure the fouling is removed from the frame face and the barrel catch. Use a dry patch to remove any residual moisture.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.41

deepSteps.title: Expose and clean the firing pin
deepSteps.action: Hold the trigger and walk the hammer forward to push the pin out, clean it, then let the hammer return to rest.
deepSteps.caution: Ease the hammer down under thumb control. Letting it snap forward on an empty breech is a dry fire.
deepSteps.quote: 11. Pull the trigger and push the hammer forward so the firing pin is exposed. Use a dry patch that has been sprayed with solvent to clean the exposed portion of the firing pin. After the firing pin has been cleaned, release the trigger and remove your thumb from the hammer. The hammer should move into the At Rest position and the firing pin should recess back into the frame.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.41

deepSteps.title: Clean the outside of the frame
deepSteps.action: Solvent and nylon-brush the frame exterior, release lever, hammer and the hammer channel.
deepSteps.quote: 12. To clean the outside of the frame, lightly spray it with solvent. Use the Nylon Brush to remove any fouling from the outside of the frame, the barrel release lever, hammer, hammer extension, and inside the hammer channel.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.41

deepSteps.title: Oil and grease the frame
deepSteps.action: Oil every metal surface inside and out, then put light grease on the pivot points.
deepSteps.quote: 13. Oil the inside and outside of the frame. Be sure to oil all metal surfaces. 14. Lightly grease the pivot points on the frame.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.42

deepSteps.title: Grease the breech plug threads
deepSteps.action: Coat the plug threads generously with breech plug grease before it goes anywhere near the barrel.
deepSteps.quote: 15. Generously lubricate the threads of the breech plug with breech plug grease. Not using the recommended lubricant will cause o-ring damage and breech plug seizure.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® PURSUIT™ XT — FIT-77 01-21 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.42
deepSteps.warn: Ordinary gun oil is not a substitute here. The manual ties the wrong lubricant directly to o-ring damage and a seized plug.

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Solvent-soak the bore for 15 minutes before scrubbing
Bronze-brush breech to muzzle and back
Dry-patch from the breech until patches come out clean
Seasoning or lubed patch muzzle to breech
Light gun oil over the barrel exterior and the extractor

cleaning.name: Breech plug
tasks: Solvent inside and out, or 10 minutes in the parts bath
Stiff-brush the outside threads and the inner area
Pipe cleaner through the fire channel
Wipe dry and repeat until no residue transfers
Grease the threads generously with breech plug grease

cleaning.name: Frame
tasks: Solvent and brush the frame interior, frame face and barrel catch
Clean the exposed firing pin, then let the hammer return to rest
Solvent and nylon-brush the exterior, release lever, hammer and hammer channel
Oil all metal surfaces inside and out
Light grease on the pivot points

reassembly: Press the barrel catch lever in, reinstall the barrel assembly onto the frame and lock it into place.
Reinstall the forend onto the barreled action and run the forend screw back in with the 4mm Allen wrench — do not overtighten.
Inspect the breech plug's fire channel is clear, then thread the lubricated plug in clockwise by finger until it seats firmly against the barrel.
If the plug will not thread smoothly or seat fully, back it out and inspect the o-ring and the threads rather than forcing it.
Reinstall the ramrod through the thimbles.
fncheck: Confirm the barrel locks up on the frame, the safety moves between red-showing and no-red, and the hammer cycles to At Rest under control. Traditions warns not to fire with excess grease or oil left in the bore — run a dry patch through before shooting.
